sampling_model.design: Four independent destructive population snapshots at times \(0,h,2h,3h\).
sampling_model.units: At time \(kh\), \(n_k\) independent units are sampled from the marginal law of \(Y_k\); no unit is followed across time.
sampling_model.treatment: No designated treatment is present; the structural target is the continuous-time interaction generator \(G\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Sample means and covariances form \(\widehat z\). On the cyclic chart, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\) and \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\). On a regular noncyclic finite branch, the local residual projection gives \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\) and \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{loc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}},\widehat z)\); globally certified initialization and labeling remain the explicit open question.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2.1 characterizes and generically selects a transition from two covariance congruences and mean equations when the propagated noise covariance is known.
Corollary 2.1 states that three time points identify the transition and constant load under its known-noise conditions.
Theorems 6 and 8 recover deterministic affine dynamics from two supplied covariance pairs and mean pairs under generic spectral and probe conditions.
Theorem 1 states that QWENDY returns the ground-truth linearized transition from four supplied covariance matrices under invertibility and simple-spectrum conditions.
Algorithms 1 and 2 alternate Schrödinger-bridge trajectory reconstruction with transition and process-noise updates for direct state snapshots.
Theorems 2 and 4 certify Newton convergence and equality or distinctness of supplied approximate roots of square polynomial systems.
The paper derives concentration and normal approximation for empirical spectral-projector error under Gaussian sampling.
Theorem 2.6 makes likelihood-ratio limits at semialgebraic boundaries and singularities depend on tangent cones.

body.tldr: Four independent Gaussian snapshots can identify a stable continuous-time linear mechanism even when every observed covariance contains the same unknown positive-definite measurement component, but the answer is a stratified fiber rather than automatically one matrix. Covariance differencing removes the common nuisance and exposes a simultaneous congruence problem; blockwise probe Gram equalities parameterize every candidate by residual orthogonal stabilizers, after which stability, the principal-logarithm cut, a Stein reconstruction, and strict noise positivity give necessary and sufficient compatibility. Three snapshots retain a continuous \(O(p-1)\) ambiguity for \(p\ge3\), whereas four identify generically through the rational map \(K_1K_0^{-1}\). The same stabilizer dimension equals information nullity, finite fibers can contain exponentially many admissible branches, and regular branches admit perturbation bounds and Gaussian moment inference. A certified data-based initializer and stable labeling rule for every noncyclic finite branch is retained as the first-class open construction problem.

project_justification.gap: Published snapshot-identification theorems either assume known propagated noise or treat the observed covariance as the latent covariance. They do not classify the compatible generator and shared unknown measurement-covariance fiber, and existing numerical methods do not certify all branches.
project_justification.niche: Common measurement noise cancels from adjacent covariance differences but re-enters through level-covariance positivity. This creates a tractable two-sided congruence geometry whose orthogonal stabilizers can be completely classified and whose regularity has a direct information interpretation.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies an if-and-only-if block Gram certificate, a bijective admissibility map, a sharp three-versus-four snapshot frontier, complete exceptional and exponential-fiber results, rational perturbation theory, branchwise inference, and a concrete \(\alpha\)-certification handle for the remaining global empirical-labeling problem.

body.related_work: AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 provides the closest proof architecture: whitening two covariance congruences leaves signs or repeated-eigenvalue orthogonal blocks, while mean differences select among them; its Theorem 2.1 assumes known process covariance and its observation-noise remark requires known subtraction. WangEtAl2024 proves a three-time-point result for deterministic affine dynamics from supplied state moments and motivates the \(\texttt{covar\_lin\_dyn}\) consumer. QWENDY2025 uses four supplied covariance matrices and simple spectra to resolve a homogeneous congruence problem, but it contains no unknown common additive covariance or complete exceptional-fiber theorem. MorimotoKashima2025 and InoueEtAl2026 estimate stochastic linear dynamics from direct snapshot marginals by Schrödinger-bridge optimization without a global common-noise identification certificate. Blevins2017 analyzes continuous-time aliases and motivates the principal-logarithm strip after the transition is recovered. KoltchinskiiLounici2017 supplies spectral perturbation tools, while HauensteinSottile2012 supplies root certificates; neither solves basis-invariant finite-branch enumeration with matrix-inequality filters. ChernozhukovHongTamer2007 and Drton2009 locate set inference and singular asymptotics around the proposed regular-stratum results. KongEtAl2023 studies process and measurement covariance identification from a paired stationary time series with known system matrices, a different information regime that confirms why destructive marginal snapshots need their own rank geometry.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Exact population spectral matching and block Gram equality must never be applied as empirical accept-or-reject tests because noisy sample moments satisfy them with probability zero. On the cyclic chart, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\) is the off-model rational estimator used by the perturbation theorem. The radius \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\) guarantees that its full plug-in reconstruction is defined, whereas the smaller radius \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\) also preserves the stability, logarithm, Stein, and reconstructed-covariance positivity filters; neither radius makes noisy moments satisfy the exact population raw equations. On a noncyclic finite stratum, the population-centered estimator \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is the local residual estimator used by the limit theorem, but it is not a globally implementable branch finder until the certified initializer and labeling question is solved. The two structural plug-ins are \(\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\) and \(\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}},\widehat z)\); each has initial-mean coordinate \(\widehat m_0\).
body.honest_scope: The population fiber, generic frontier, stabilizer dimension, attained exponential multiplicity, information-nullity identity, cyclic perturbation bounds, and local regular-branch limit law are theorem targets. The global certified initializer, completeness certificate, stable empirical labeling, and simultaneous coverage across all noncyclic finite branches remain open. No uniform inference is claimed at branch collisions, positivity boundaries, logarithm cuts, or stabilizer-dimension jumps. Bit complexity for algebraic spectral decomposition and exact matrix logarithms is outside the arithmetic-workload claim. When \(E\) is supplied, the separate fiber \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{known}}(E)\) uses exact level-covariance congruences and the equality \(E_W=E\), and its three-snapshot restriction reduces to AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022. For \(p=2\), the determinant and logarithm filters can remove the generic three-snapshot reflection, so the three-snapshot lower bound is deliberately restricted to \(p\ge3\).
